10 استوحش : see 5. ―
-b2- It is also quasi-pass. of أَوْحَشَ الرَّجُلَ, (S, TA,) and [thus] signifies He felt, or experienced, وَحْشَة [i. e. loneliness, or solitude, &c.; and sadness, grief, sorrow, or disquietude or trouble of mind, &c.; and fear, &c.]. (S, * K, TA.) And استوحش إِلَى الشَّىْءِ [He felt a want of the thing]. (K, voce عُرِىَ, q. v.) You say also استوحش مِنْهُ, (A, TA,) or عَنْهُ, (Msb,) [meaning He was afraid of, or feared, him, or it; agreeably with an explanation of the inf. n. in Har, p. 331: see also an instance below, voce وَحْشٌ: or] meaning he was shy of him; averse from him; unsocial, unsociable, or unfamiliar, with him; and like a wild animal. (TA.) ―
-b3- استوحشت الأَرْضُ: see 4. ＝
-A2- [He deemed a word, or sound, &c., strange, or uncouth.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
